messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a customer report where streaming responses get 'chopped' mid-toolcall and the console shows two token charges. Repro notes incoming.
samir: ugh. do we have a repro trace? which routing path and fallback happened?
maya: short repro: client starts a streaming generation -> model A (region-us) gets a toolcall -> during toolcall we hit a preflight capacity error so routing falls back to model B (region-eu) which returns truncated stream and then a resumed stream from B. Console shows A tokens + B tokens.
oliver: that sounds like double-charging due to overlapping accounting windows. Is the toolcall counted when the call is initiated or when the server commits the tokens?
samir: today we charge tokens at final emission + best-effort provisional for streaming prefixes. Fallbacks weren't updating the provisional ledger when we abandoned A.
chloe: so the UX shows total tokens billed = A_emitted + B_emitted, even though user only got B final?
maya: exactly. customer sees inflated usage and the per-route dashboard attributes tokens to both route=A and route=B which is what triggered support ticket.
oliver: can we avoid provisional commits on routes until we confirm a non-fallback path? i.e., buffer provisional accounting locally per-request and only flush on final ack?
samir: buffering would reduce real-time visibility though — console metrics and rate limit enforcement rely on provisional numbers for SLOs. If we delay flush, quotas could be bypassed during long streams.
chloe: maybe a hybrid: keep provisional for quota enforcement but mark them as "tentative" in billing table and reconcile on final completion. Console should show tentative vs charged.
maya: agree. but reconciliation must handle retries where the same tokens are re-emitted after truncation (we need idempotency). The tricky bit: toolcall tokens are sometimes generated by the model mid-stream and can be truncated by client but replayed after fallback.
oliver: we already have request_id + stream_position in headers. Could use a per-request accounting idempotency token; when fallback happens, the fallback stream references the same accounting id and we dedupe on final commit.
samir: implementation notes: 1) add accounting_id to stream init and all toolcall events 2) provisional ledger records accounting_id -> (route, tentative_tokens) 3) final commit operation marks accounting_id charged with final route and token delta 4) reconciliation job sweeps tentatives older than X and resolves conflicts.
chloe: what about telemetry? dashboards need to show both tentative and committed so ops can see when reconciliation is in-flight. We should add a "tentative_tokens" series to per-route time series and a reconciled_tokens series.
maya: +1. Also need a UX change: in per-route view, show a note when >1% of tokens in window are tentative so SREs know there were fallbacks.
oliver: edge case: what if fallback model emits more tokens for same input (longer completion) — dedupe won't reduce that; we need to ensure user is billed for final emitted tokens only. So final commit should replace tentative amount, not sum.
samir: agreed. commit semantics: replace tentative with committed for that accounting_id. If commit route differs, move attribution to final route.
chloe: any perf concerns? provisional writes are hot. Could use in-memory cache with async write to ledger and fallback-safe replay log.
maya: let's prototype: samir + oliver pair on Friday to implement accounting_id plumbing; i'll update Console PR to render tentative vs committed charts and a flag in per-route header.
oliver: ping deploy-bot for a canary once prototype passes unit tests.
deploy-bot: deploy started for branch token-accounting/fallback-reconcile to canary env (canary-3). Logs: 200 OK, 3 instances.
samir: test cases to add: simultaneous multi-region fallback, mid-toolcall abort + retry, reconciling out-of-order commits. Also add e2e across private deployment (customers reported this on private infra).
maya: thanks. Filed follow-up RFC in #eng-platform-docs with design + reconciliation window defaults. Will include migration plan for historical tentative rows.
chloe: quick note — for billing export, ensure tentative rows are not exported to billing CSVs until committed. Support needs a view to show tentative breakdown per customer during reconciliation window.
maya: yep. I'll loop in support and finance.
oliver: cool. if we keep the accounting_id approach, we can also use it to make streaming rate-limit decisions more accurate.
samir: okay locking in approach. I'll create PRs for runtime and ledger schema tomorrow.
